reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses thermal stress-induced cracking in an Al-HEA coating, not the native oxide on Q235 steel, and attributes cracking to internal stresses, not thermal expansion mismatch. It provides no support for the key premises about Q235's oxide film behavior or the corrosion mechanism.
premises: Thermal stresses induce microcracking in the native oxide film on Q235 steel at elevated temperatures.
Microcracking of the oxide film exposes fresh metal to aggressive species, triggering localized galvanic corrosion.
An intact oxide film suppresses corrosion-related degradation.
Differences in thermal expansion between the steel substrate and its oxide cause stress build-up.
